explanations: luna: When Moses strikes the rock, twelve springs burst forth; “ٱنفَجَرَتْ” is the section's secondary water sense of ف ج ر, here supplying a people rather than a garden. | terra: فَٱنفَجَرَتْ مِنْهُ ٱثْنَتَا عَشْرَةَ عَيْنًا uses the fecr branch for water bursting from rock and assigns each people its drinking-place, joining eruption with apportioned access.

luna: Righteousness includes giving wealth, despite love for it, to relatives, orphans, and the needy; this makes the section's wealth and orphan images meet in the opposite act of generosity. | terra: True righteousness includes giving wealth despite loving it to orphans and the poor, reversing both attachment to wealth and refusal of the orphan's table.

luna: Dawn is distinguished as the white thread from the black thread of night; this makes the section's image of dawn emerging through darkness concrete. | terra: The white thread of dawn becoming distinct from the black thread presents daybreak as a visible separation from darkness, closely matching the section's rending of the night-cover.
terra: The answer about spending directs good wealth to parents, kin, orphans, the poor, and travelers, turning possession toward a broad shared table.

luna: On orphans the verse says that mixing with them makes them “your brothers”; this gives concrete support to the section's image of honoring the lone orphan by joining and backing him. | terra: The command concerning orphans says وَإِن تُخَالِطُوهُمْ فَإِخْوَٰنُكُمْ; mixing with them as brothers directly answers the image of the orphan as a person with nobody beside him.

luna: Abraham asks for a sign of resurrection “لِيَطْمَئِنَّ قَلْبِي”; the related root gives a concrete parallel to the section's reassured soul at the threshold of the afterlife. | terra: Abraham asks to see how the dead are revived so that his heart may become tranquil, showing طمأنينة as settled trust rather than attachment to present goods.

terra: Love of amassed gold, livestock, and cultivation is named as the enjoyment of lower life, while the best return is with God; beloved property and the journey's true endpoint are placed together.
terra: What is better than those possessions is then named as gardens and pleasure from God, moving directly from wealth-love to garden and divine رضوان.
terra: One cannot attain righteousness until spending from what one loves, a direct ethical reversal of clinging to beloved wealth.
terra: God makes the angelic reinforcement only good news and a means for hearts to become tranquil, bringing angels and inward settling into the same scene.
luna: People who withhold God's bounty must not think it good for them; what they withheld becomes a collar on the Resurrection Day, reversing the section's claim that wealth proves honor.

luna: The verse forbids mixing good property with bad and consuming orphan wealth with one's own; it directly illuminates the section's image of swallowing another's inheritance into one's private heap. | terra: The command to return orphan property and not consume it into one's own wealth directly exposes the section's image of swallowing another person's share into a solitary heap.
terra: The guardians must test orphans, deliver their property at maturity, and avoid consuming it wastefully or hastily, specifying the restraint absent from the section's indiscriminate eating.

luna: Men and women each have an allotted share of what parents and kin leave; this is the division the section says is erased when inheritance is gulped down whole. | terra: Men and women each have نَصِيبٌ مَّفْرُوضٌ from what relatives leave; fixed shares form the legal boundary against eating an inheritance without division.

luna: When inheritance is being divided, needy relatives, orphans, and the poor who are present are to receive provision and kind words; this directly joins the section's inheritance shares, orphan, and table images. | terra: When relatives, orphans, and the poor attend the division, they are to be provided and addressed kindly, turning inheritance-sharing itself into the section's communal table.

luna: Those who consume orphan property unjustly are said to consume fire into their bellies; it gives the moral consequence of the inheritance-hoarding the section depicts. | terra: Those who consume orphan wealth unjustly are described as eating fire into their bellies, making the hidden reality of the section's indiscriminate inheritance-eating concrete.
luna: This verse assigns inheritance portions to children and parents; its detailed shares continue 4:7's principle, the precise opposite of clearing an inheritance without division.
luna: Spousal and sibling shares are assigned here, continuing the same legal division and clarifying the multiple claims erased by a single hoard.

terra: The command to serve God lists the orphan and poor together with the near neighbor, distant neighbor, and companion at one's side, concretely answering unsupported singleness with people who come alongside.
terra: The disciples ask whether their Lord can send down a table from heaven; it supplies the actual table whose purpose is inward reassurance in 5:113.
terra: The disciples say the descending table will let them eat and تَطْمَئِنَّ قُلُوبُنَا; the table-image and inward tranquility meet explicitly here.

luna: This verse joins God's pleasure with theirs to entry into gardens; the mutual honor comes from truth and divine approval, reversing the section's claim that wealth proves honor. | terra: رَّضِىَ ٱللَّهُ عَنْهُمْ وَرَضُوا۟ عَنْهُ follows gardens with abiding residence, another exact Quranic expansion of reciprocal pleasure.
luna: When a people forget the warning, they are given abundance before being seized suddenly; this is a specific reversal of treating plentiful provision as proof of divine favor.
terra: God's ability to send punishment from above or from beneath the feet frames the vertical boundary of the section's descending scourge and leveled ground.
terra: فَلَمَّا جَنَّ عَلَيْهِ ٱلَّيْلُ uses the j-n-n branch for night covering Abraham, making audible the covering sense that the section finds in جنتي.

luna: People come to God singly, leaving their possessions behind and finding no intercessors; this is the section's solitary person without anyone to stand beside or support him. | terra: وَلَقَدْ جِئْتُمُونَا فُرَادَىٰ depicts every person arriving singly, with possessions and alleged partners left behind, exactly the solitude the section opposes to entry among God's servants.

luna: God is “فَالِقُ الْإِصْبَاحِ”, cleaving daybreak from night; it gives a direct parallel to the section's opening dawn breaking a covering of darkness. | terra: فَالِقُ ٱلْإِصْبَاحِ and the night made for rest present daybreak as a splitting that ends the dark covering, the first half of the section's cover-image.
terra: Iblis vows to sit for people on God's straight path, a hostile literal road-ambush that contrasts with divine judgment stationed at the unavoidable watchpoint.
luna: Adam and his spouse use leaves of the Garden as a covering; the ayah makes concrete the section's meeting of the Garden word with the cover of trees.
terra: ٱدْخُلُوا۟ ٱلْجَنَّةَ لَا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْكُمْ addresses people once denied mercy and calls them into the garden without fear or grief, another restorative entry scene.

luna: Winds drive heavy clouds and rain revives a dead land; this concrete rain-bearing cloud is the merciful counterpart to the cloud over Ad's valley. | terra: A heavy cloud is driven to dead land and sends down water that brings every fruit forth, providing the merciful cloud-outcome that Ad wrongly expected in 46:24.
terra: The rain sent upon Lot's people is punitive rather than life-giving, a repeated Quranic reversal of the rain hoped for from a cloud.

luna: In another account of Moses, water issues from a struck rock for twelve tribes; it repeats the section's meeting of a spring and a people, though this wording uses a different root from its named ف ج ر sense. | terra: Twelve springs gush from the struck rock and every tribe knows its drinking-place, a repeated non-f-j-r wording of water opened and apportioned for servants.

terra: وَلَٰكِنَّهُۥٓ أَخْلَدَ إِلَى ٱلْأَرْضِ depicts a person clinging durably to earth and then gives an animal likeness, directly illuminating the section's wealth-lover settled like an animal that will not rise.
terra: The repeated formulation says the angelic support is good news so that hearts may become tranquil, again pairing angels with the calm later addressed as a soul.
terra: A fixed share of acquired wealth is assigned to kin, orphans, the poor, and travelers, another distributive counter-scene to swallowing all shares into one heap.

luna: The verse uses the ambush form “مَرْصَدٍ” for those lying in wait on roads; it gives a human road-side instance of the section's ambush-word, while reversing the divine watcher into people waiting for opponents. | terra: وَٱقْعُدُوا۟ لَهُمْ كُلَّ مَرْصَدٍ uses the same r-s-d branch for literal watchers stationed at every ambush-place, clarifying the spatial force of مرصاد in the section.
luna: Those who hoard gold and silver and do not spend it in God's cause are warned of painful punishment; the verse directly links a person's stored wealth with what will not save him.
luna: The hoarded metals are heated in Hell and used to brand their owners; this neighboring detail makes the consequence of 9:34's wealth-hoarding bodily and inescapable.

luna: When called to set out, people “اثَّاقَلْتُمْ إِلَى الْأَرْضِ” and prefer this world's life; the section uses this exact earth-clinging image as the contrary of the tranquil soul's return to its Lord. | terra: ٱثَّاقَلْتُمْ إِلَى ٱلْأَرْضِ and أَرَضِيتُم بِٱلْحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا put becoming heavy toward earth and being satisfied with the nearer life in the same rebuke, the section's exact foil to the returning, mutually pleased soul.
terra: ٱنفِرُوا۟ خِفَافًا وَثِقَالًا commands both light and heavy to set out and spend wealth and life, reversing the earthbound attachment rebuked in 9:38.

luna: The earliest believers and those who follow them are gathered in the account of mutual pleasure and Gardens; this is a specific group-entry parallel to the section's soul admitted among God's servants. | terra: God's pleasure with the first believers and their pleasure with Him is followed by prepared gardens, repeating the section's pleasure-to-entry relation.

luna: Those who do not expect to meet God are “رَضُوا بِالْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا وَاطْمَأَنُّوا بِهَا”; their contentment and settledness in this life directly reverse the section's soul returning contentedly to its Lord. | terra: Those who are رَضُوا۟ بِٱلْحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا وَٱطْمَأَنُّوا۟ بِهَا combine satisfaction and tranquility in the lower life; this is the precise false rest reversed by the soul pleased with its Lord.
luna: Their earned destination is the Fire; this neighboring consequence completes 10:7's contentment with worldly life and contrasts with the Garden awaiting the returning soul.
luna: After the flood, earth is told to swallow its water and the sky to stop; the waters subside and the ark settles, a measured ending to the overflow named in the section.
terra: Lot's settlement is turned upside down and followed with a rain of marked baked stones, joining leveling, descent from above, and rain transformed into punishment.
luna: Joseph asks to die submitted and be joined with the righteous; this gives another specific formulation of the section's soul welcomed into a community at the end of its journey.
terra: God raises the heavens بِغَيْرِ عَمَدٍۢ تَرَوْنَهَا; the enduring divine elevation without visible columns is a boundary to the human stone columns the section sees leveled.

terra: Water descends, valleys carry it according to their measure, and the flood bears rising foam while what benefits people remains; this is a precise boundary between measured flow and transgressive overflow.

luna: Hearts “تَطْمَئِنُّ” through remembrance of God; that related root and stated cause give a concrete parallel to the section's soul made calm after upheaval. | terra: أَلَا بِذِكْرِ ٱللَّهِ تَطْمَئِنُّ ٱلْقُلُوبُ locates true settling in remembrance, supplying the inward sense of the addressed ٱلنَّفْسُ ٱلْمُطْمَئِنَّةُ.
luna: The Garden's food is lasting and its shade enduring; this supports the section's meeting of the Garden word with tree-cover, while the section's 76:6 link supplies the gushing spring.
terra: Those who prefer the lower life also obstruct God's path and seek it crooked; worldly preference is thus joined to blocking the journey the soul should make.
terra: The earth is replaced by another earth, the heavens likewise, and everyone emerges before the One; transformed ground and universal appearance meet in a single judgment scene.
terra: The God-fearing are among gardens and springs immediately before the entry-call, supplying both destination and water.
terra: ٱدْخُلُوهَا بِسَلَٰمٍ ءَامِنِينَ calls them into that garden setting in peace and security, close to the call heard by the tranquil soul.
terra: The same destruction is restated as making the town's high part its low part and raining baked stones, an exact meeting of lowering and punitive precipitation.
terra: The roof falls on plotters مِن فَوْقِهِمْ and punishment reaches them from where they do not perceive; this joins collapsed construction, descent from above, and an ambush-like arrival.
terra: A heart that remains tranquil in faith under compulsion shows inward طمأنينة persisting despite outward pressure.
terra: Their disbelief is explained by preferring the lower life to the hereafter, another direct statement of the choice reversed by the soul's return.
terra: A town once ءَامِنَةً مُّطْمَئِنَّةً with provision from every place tastes hunger and fear after ingratitude, showing that outward ease and provision are a tested, reversible tranquility.
terra: The command not to approach orphan wealth except in the best manner until maturity gives another explicit boundary against absorbing the orphan's share.

terra: God declares that He has honored all children of Adam, carried them on land and sea, and provided them with good things, joining true honor, provision, and journey without making wealth its criterion.

luna: The disbelievers demand that the Prophet make a spring gush from earth (“تُفَجِّرَ لَنَا”); the same ف ج ر water sense is framed as a demand, unlike the spring assigned for the servants in the section's 76:6 link. | terra: The demand that Muhammad تَفْجُرَ لَنَا مِنَ ٱلْأَرْضِ يَنۢبُوعًا preserves the fecr-root's spring-opening sense without yet adding the garden supplied in 17:91.
terra: The demanded garden of palms and vines must have rivers burst through it تَفْجِيرًا, bringing garden and the fecr-root's gushing-water sense into one scene.

luna: The section's stated water sense of ف ج ر appears in “فَجَّرْنَا خِلَالَهُمَا نَهَرًا”: a river is made to flow through two gardens, joining its spring-water and garden images. | terra: Between two fruitful gardens God causes a river to burst forth, وَفَجَّرْنَا خِلَٰلَهُمَا نَهَرًا, another exact meeting of garden covering and fecr as water-opening.
luna: The owner of one of the two gardens boasts that he has greater wealth and more people; this closely stages the section's person who reads abundance as proof of being honored.

luna: Entering his garden, the owner assumes it will never perish and doubts the Hour; this joins garden and wealth to a false belief in permanence, against the section's passing structures and lasting return.

luna: The garden's water sinks into the earth so its owner cannot recover it; this is a precise reversal of the section's spring that servants can direct within the Garden. | terra: The worldly garden's water may sink so deep that its owner cannot seek it, reversing the secure spring within the final garden.
luna: The garden is ruined and its owner regrets what he spent on it; this brings the section's themes of wealth, earth, and belated regret into one scene.
luna: No group can help the garden's owner against God; this is an exact social counterpart to the section's person arriving alone without anyone to support him.
luna: After the garden owner loses it and has no helper, the passage declares that protection belongs to God, the True; this gives a fitting answer to the section's return to the Lord.

luna: Wealth and children are called adornments of worldly life, while lasting good deeds are better; the verse supplies the boundary against reading abundance as the honor the section's wealthy person claims. | terra: Wealth and children are adornment of the lower life, whereas lasting good deeds are better with the Lord in reward and hope; what passes and what remains are weighed against one another.

luna: The mountains are moved and earth appears level, while all people are gathered; this unites the section's flattened ground and the arrival of beings upon it. | terra: The mountains are moved, the earth appears bare, and all are gathered without exception; this supplies the cleared ground on which the next ayah's row is formed.
terra: وَعُرِضُوا۟ عَلَىٰ رَبِّكَ صَفًّا places the gathered people in a row before the Lord on the exposed earth of 18:47, closely matching leveling followed by ordered ranks.
terra: The statement that every one of the addressees will come to Hell, an outcome decreed by the Lord, supplies the compulsory passage implicit in Hell as an ambush-place.
terra: The next ayah distinguishes those rescued from those left kneeling there, adding the moral boundary to the unavoidable passage announced in 19:71.
terra: The boastful owner is stripped of what he names and comes to God فَرْدًا, joining wealth's loss to the resurrection singleness described by the section.
terra: Every being in the heavens and earth comes to the Merciful as a servant before 19:95 says each comes singly, placing shared servant-status and individual arrival side by side.

luna: Every person comes to God alone on the Day of Resurrection; this repeats the section's solitary arrival, while its other image offers entry among the servants as the answer to aloneness. | terra: وَكُلُّهُمْ ءَاتِيهِ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ فَرْدًا repeats the resurrection arrival as an individual, sharpening the section's pair-versus-single image.
terra: The question about the mountains is answered by their being blown away, supplying the removal that produces the صفصف plain in 20:106.

luna: The section cites this verse's mountains scattered until the land is left level; its “صَفْصَفًا” is the same dictionary word the section derives from ص ف ف for a level plain. | terra: فَيَذَرُهَا قَاعًا صَفْصَفًا is the section's named level plain, whose صف-derived name prepares the ground for ranks.

luna: The land is so level that no depression or elevation remains; this neighboring detail completes the plain produced by the scattered mountains in 20:106 and marks the boundary after upheaval. | terra: The level plain has neither crookedness nor elevation, defining the exact flatness on which the section imagines the ranks standing.
terra: The angels are called عِبَادٌ مُّكْرَمُونَ, bringing honored status, servant identity, and the beings who stand in ranks into one formulation.
terra: The lifeless earth quivers and swells when water descends, repeating the image of low still ground whose calm is not mere death.
terra: The person on the edge becomes tranquil when good reaches him but turns away when tested; this conditional calm exactly exposes the mistaken reading of ease as honor.
terra: يُصَبُّ مِن فَوْقِ رُءُوسِهِمُ ٱلْحَمِيمُ gives the section's vertical action precisely, though this ayah names poured boiling water rather than a poured scourge.
terra: Water descends from heaven بِقَدَرٍ and is lodged in the earth, presenting the controlled provision against which transgressive flood and freely directed garden spring are heard.
terra: The measured water of 23:18 produces gardens of palms and grapes, joining proportioned water to garden provision.
luna: At death the wrongdoer asks to be returned so he can act rightly; this is the unfulfilled return-wish opposite the section's soul welcomed back and already inside the Garden.
luna: The requested return is refused and a barrier remains until resurrection; this completes 23:99 and sharpens the section's contrast with a return granted to the contented soul.

luna: Clouds are driven, joined, and piled before rain and hail descend; this gives a volatile rain-cloud scene beside the section's cloud that appears to promise water but brings punishment. | terra: God drives and joins clouds into a mass, rain emerges through it, and hail from heaven strikes or turns away by His will; one cloud scene contains both hoped-for water and a potentially destructive descent.
luna: Winds are sent as glad tidings before mercy here, a direct reversal of the section's cloud that looks like rain but carries punishment.
luna: The water from heaven gives life to dead land and drink to people and livestock; 25:48 introduces the merciful winds, contrasting Ad's cloud and punishment.

luna: The section's word عَذَاب is paired in its prose with the sweet-water sense of ع ذ ب; this verse calls one of two seas “عَذْبٌ فُرَاتٌ”, making the hoped-for taste concrete beside the other, salty water. | terra: هَٰذَا عَذْبٌ فُرَاتٌ names fresh sweet water with عذب, the lexical branch the section sets against the عذاب that arrived instead of rain.
terra: وَأَمْطَرْنَا عَلَيْهِم مَّطَرًا calls a destructive visitation rain, a specific reversal of the life-giving rain expected from a cloud.
luna: Solomon asks to be admitted by God's mercy among His righteous servants; this is a close prayer-form parallel to the section's call for the soul to enter among the servants.

terra: Solomon calls the gift before him a test of whether he will give thanks, and affirms that his Lord is self-sufficient and generous; possession is thus trial rather than proof of personal honor.
terra: The same destructive rain is called evil for those who had been warned, reinforcing rain's specific reversal into retribution.
terra: Pharaoh commands Haman to fire clay and make a tower so that he can rise toward Moses' God, another doomed act of human vertical building.
terra: Whatever people receive is only lower-life enjoyment and adornment, while what is with God is better and lasting, another boundary around wealth's apparent honor.
luna: Qarun is introduced with treasures so heavy their keys burden a group; this is a vivid individual heap of wealth against the section's account of wealth-love.
luna: Qarun is told to seek the Hereafter with what God has given him, do good, and not spread corruption; this directly corrects the section's image of wealth used for hoarding rather than care.
luna: Qarun claims his fortune comes from his own knowledge; this self-grounding, answered by his downfall in 28:81, parallels the section's wealthy person reading possessions as proof of honor.
luna: Qarun appears in his adornment, and people who desire worldly life wish they had what he received; this stages the section's mistaken reading of visible wealth as honor.

luna: Those with knowledge answer that God's reward is better for the patient; this corrects the admiration of Qarun's wealth in 28:79 and echoes the section's distinction between possessions and genuine honor.

luna: The earth swallows Qarun and his house, showing that the wealth-laden figure is not held up by the ground or saved by his possessions. | terra: Qarun and his house are swallowed by the earth, and neither his supporting party nor he can save him; accumulated wealth ends in literal earthboundness without a supporter.

luna: Onlookers realize that God expands or restricts provision as He wills; this corrects the assumption that riches prove honor, completing Qarun's downfall in 28:81. | terra: The former envier of Qarun now recognizes that God expands and restricts provision and that worldly success did not signify favor, directly correcting the section's two claims about provision.
terra: Punishment covers them from above and from beneath their feet, spatially developing the section's overhead recompense at the traveler's unavoidable ground.
luna: The ayah describes winds raising and spreading clouds until rain emerges; it gives the merciful version of the cloud that Ad mistake for rain in the section's cited 46:24.
luna: The people rejoice after having despaired before the rain; this neighboring response makes explicit the hope and reversal that the section contrasts with Ad's false expectation.
luna: The rain leaves traces of mercy by reviving dead earth; this is the saving effect of the cloud in 30:48, opposite the destruction that arrives under Ad's cloud.
terra: The same creation claim, heavens raised بِغَيْرِ عَمَدٍۢ تَرَوْنَهَا, repeats the contrast between divine support and doomed human monumental supports.
terra: Neither parent nor child can avail the other on the promised day, specifying the severance of even the closest human support.
terra: Two gardens, wholesome land, and the command to eat the Lord's provision present paired garden-cover as a received gift rather than personal proof of rank.
terra: When the people turn away, the flood of the dam is sent and their two gardens are exchanged for bitter growth, joining destructive overflow with the loss of garden-cover and provision.

luna: This second water contrast names one sea “عَذْبٌ فُرَاتٌ” and the other bitter; it supports the section's explicit wordplay between عَذَاب and sweet water without confusing the two meanings. | terra: The repeated هَٰذَا عَذْبٌ فُرَاتٌ contrasts drinkable sweetness with the punishment-sense carried by the nearly same letters in the cloud scene.

luna: After being told to enter the Garden, the slain believer wishes his people knew; his “يَا لَيْتَ قَوْمِي يَعْلَمُونَ” is an after-entry wish, unlike the section's regretful wish to have prepared beforehand. | terra: قِيلَ ٱدْخُلِ ٱلْجَنَّةَ places the faithful man inside the garden before his wish, directly paralleling the soul's invitation to enter while reversing the condemned man's belated wish.

luna: The speaker says his Lord made him one of the honored after forgiving him; this neighboring ayah grounds the section's contrast between honor inferred from wealth and honor received through forgiveness. | terra: His wish concerns his Lord's forgiveness and making him مِنَ ٱلْمُكْرَمِينَ, relocating honor from wealth to pardon and admission exactly as the section explains.

luna: The section's garden and the secondary water sense of ف ج ر meet in “وَفَجَّرْنَا فِيهَا مِنَ الْعُيُونِ”, where springs are made to gush within gardens of palms and grapes. | terra: Gardens of palms and grapes are paired with وَفَجَّرْنَا فِيهَا مِنَ ٱلْعُيُونِ, explicitly placing burst springs inside gardens.
terra: After the gardens and burst springs of 36:34, the Creator of all pairs is praised; paired creation, garden, and gushing water thus meet in one continuous passage.
luna: The opening oath names those who are ranged in rows; the section's repeated صفّ imagery likewise leaves angelic ranks standing after the built structures fall.
terra: فَوَٰكِهُ وَهُم مُّكْرَمُونَ places being honored amid garden provision, opposing the claim that worldly wealth itself proves honor.
terra: The honored recipients of fruit in 37:42 are located here in gardens of bliss; this ayah supplies the garden setting before 37:44 seats them facing one another.
terra: عَلَىٰ سُرُرٍۢ مُّتَقَٰبِلِينَ seats the honored people face to face, a concrete afterlife reversal of the orphan's unsupported singleness.
terra: The angels say each of them has a known station, specifying the ordered places from which they declare themselves the row-makers in 37:165.
terra: The angels say وَإِنَّا لَنَحْنُ ٱلصَّآفُّونَ, identifying ordered standing in ranks as their own characteristic stance.

terra: The ayah refuses to equate believers and righteous workers with makers of فساد or to equate the God-fearing with الفجار, explicitly joining the surah's corruption theme to the moral f-j-r branch.

luna: The God-fearing are brought to the Garden in groups; that communal entry answers the section's single orphan image with the soul entering among God's servants. | terra: The garden's keepers say فَٱدْخُلُوهَا خَٰلِدِينَ to the God-fearing brought in groups; entry here is explicitly communal rather than solitary.
terra: The entrants praise God for giving them the land to settle wherever they wish in the garden, presenting chosen settlement after the journey rather than being stuck to the lower earth.
terra: The angels are seen surrounding the Throne in praise when judgment is completed, a circular angelic ordering rather than the section's straight ranks.

luna: The section's fallen columns and stakes gain a related image in Pharaoh's order to build a tower reaching toward heaven; this ayah makes his vertical construction an expression of the same worldly reach. | terra: Pharaoh orders Haman to build him a lofty structure, extending the doomed monumentality already carried by Pharaoh's pegs.

luna: The next ayah completes the tower episode by exposing Pharaoh's plot as futile; it gives the section's human-built height a specific limit in Pharaoh's own context. | terra: He states that the tower is meant to reach the ways of heaven and then calls Moses a liar, exposing the self-exalting aim of that raised construction.
luna: Aad are punished by a cold, furious wind over days of misery; it is another account of the wind that turns the hoped-for cloud into destruction.

terra: The earth is seen خَٰشِعَةً, then quivers and swells when water descends; its low stillness is not death, offering a natural counterpart to the soul lowered yet alive and responsive after upheaval.
terra: Water descends from heaven according to measure and revives a dead land, presenting beneficial measured descent against the cloud that carries destruction.
terra: يَٰعِبَادِ لَا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْكُمُ ٱلْيَوْمَ addresses God's servants with reassurance at the last day, closely matching the peaceful call that gathers the soul among the servants.
terra: The intervening ayah identifies those servants by faith and submission, specifying who receives the reassurance of 43:68 and entry of 43:70.
terra: ٱدْخُلُوا۟ ٱلْجَنَّةَ calls those servants and their spouses into the garden together, joining entry, community, and the pair-image.

luna: The source section explicitly links the verb صَبَّ, a water-pouring action, to a lash of عَذَاب; this verse commands that boiling punishment be poured over a head, bringing water and torment together in its own scene. | terra: ثُمَّ صُبُّوا۟ فَوْقَ رَأْسِهِ مِنْ عَذَابِ ٱلْحَمِيمِ joins pouring, from above, and punishment in one command, making explicit the section's threefold image.

luna: The section's cloud over Ad's valleys is the cloud its people take for a rain-bearing one; the ayah corrects that expectation with “رِيحٌ فِيهَا عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ”. | terra: The people of Ad see a cloud approaching their valleys and call it rain, but are told it is the painful punishment they hastened; this is the section's exact meeting of expected sweet water, an overhead mass, and arriving عذاب.

luna: The preceding cloud's punishment is realized here as a wind that “تُدَمِّرُ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ”; this supplies the destructive force behind the section's cloud-to-judgment meeting. | terra: The next ayah identifies the apparent rain cloud as a wind that destroys everything by its Lord's command, completing the destructive arrival announced in 46:24.
terra: God is pleased with the believers and sends ٱلسَّكِينَةَ upon them beneath the tree; divine pleasure, settled calm, and living cover meet in one scene.
terra: إِنَّ أَكْرَمَكُمْ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ أَتْقَىٰكُمْ states the criterion of honor before God, directly correcting the wealth-based claim of being honored.
terra: The garden is brought near to the God-fearing, setting the destination immediately before the returning heart and peaceful entry of 50:33-34.
terra: هَٰذَا مَا تُوعَدُونَ لِكُلِّ أَوَّابٍ حَفِيظٍ identifies the recipient as one who repeatedly returns, preparing the heart's arrival in 50:33.
terra: The promised person comes بِقَلْبٍ مُّنِيبٍ, a returning heart, supplying the inward return immediately before the command to enter in peace.
terra: ٱدْخُلُوهَا بِسَلَٰمٍ is the same gardenward call with peace that the section hears addressed to the tranquil soul.
terra: ضَيْفِ إِبْرَٰهِيمَ ٱلْمُكْرَمِينَ calls Abraham's visitors honored guests, placing ikram in the social setting of receiving people at one's table.
terra: Abraham turns to his household and brings a roasted calf, supplying the meal through which the honored-guest relation of 51:24 becomes concrete.
luna: A barren wind is sent against Aad; this repeated account supports the destructive side of the section's rain-cloud encounter.
luna: The wind leaves nothing it reaches without making it like decayed remains; this neighboring result completes 51:41's barren storm.
terra: The claim that all things are created in pairs supplies the broad Quranic horizon of the section's pair image, though it does not itself depict the solitary orphan.
terra: Even if the deniers saw a piece of sky falling, they would call it سَحَابٌ مَّرْكُومٌ, directly joining the misread cloud, the descending mass, and their fatal refusal to recognize it.
terra: وَأَنَّ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ ٱلْمُنتَهَىٰ states that the final endpoint is to the Lord, supporting the return-call as completion of a journey.

luna: The section joins water descending in a flood with punishment; this flood account opens heaven's gates with pouring water, and 54:12 completes the scene with springs bursting from earth and the waters meeting. | terra: The opened gates of heaven release مَآءٍۢ مُّنْهَمِرٍۢ, staging punishment as a mass of water pouring down from above.

luna: The section's stated water sense of the root ف ج ر meets “فَجَّرْنَا الْأَرْضَ عُيُونًا”; the verse's springs rise from earth and meet the rain of 54:11, making the upper and lower waters one flood. | terra: Springs are burst from the earth and the two waters meet عَلَىٰٓ أَمْرٍۢ قَدْ قُدِرَ; it joins the fecr-root's water sense to the destructive flood while retaining divine measure.
terra: فِيهِمَا عَيْنَانِ تَجْرِيَانِ gives the paired gardens two flowing springs, combining the pair-image with controlled paradise water.
terra: فِيهِمَا عَيْنَانِ نَضَّاخَتَانِ depicts two gushing springs within the paired gardens, another measured counterpart to the flood.
luna: The earth is shaken with a mighty shaking on the final day, echoing the repeated crushing of earth in the section's judgment scene.

luna: The mountains are crushed and pulverized; this follows the earthquake in 56:4 and develops the flattening of the judgment landscape. | terra: وَبُسَّتِ ٱلْجِبَالُ بَسًّا stages the mountains crushed to pieces in the final upheaval, a close nonlexical parallel to the earth's repeated pounding.

luna: The mountains become scattered dust, completing the land's upheaval in 56:4 and 56:5 before the section's aligned ranks appear. | terra: The crushed mountains become scattered dust, completing the removal of upright mass begun in 56:5.
terra: مَآءٍ مَّسْكُوبٍ places poured water among the garden provisions of the companions of the right, restoring pouring to life-giving hospitality.
terra: The section treats جنة as tree-cover; جُنَّةً here means a shield made from oaths, a plausible same-root witness to covering, though the ayah does not depict a garden.

luna: The verse joins a community identified as God's party, entry into Gardens, and mutual divine pleasure; it repeats the section's linked images of entering among servants and being pleased with one's Lord. | terra: رَّضِىَ ٱللَّهُ عَنْهُمْ وَرَضُوا۟ عَنْهُ is paired with gardens and membership in حِزْبُ ٱللَّهِ, connecting reciprocal pleasure to entry into a gathered company.
terra: Public wealth is assigned to kin, orphans, the poor, and travelers so that it does not circulate only among the rich, a direct distributive boundary against a lone accumulating heap.

terra: وَلْتَنظُرْ نَفْسٌ مَّا قَدَّمَتْ لِغَدٍ commands every soul to inspect what it has sent ahead, directly supplying the timely counterpart to the last-day regret over failing to prepare for life.

luna: The section leaves angelic ranks standing after structures are flattened; this verse likens believers arranged in ranks to a compact building, a human formation that joins rank and structure in a contrasting way. | terra: A rank صَفًّا is likened to بُنْيَانٌ مَّرْصُوصٌ; the ayah fuses the section's surviving row with its fallen architectural image.
terra: Taking oaths as جُنَّةً repeats the shield or cover sense that supports the section's semantic hearing of garden as tree-cover.
terra: The warning that one in heaven may send a stone-bearing storm against the addressees is another specific overhead arrival of punishment.
terra: The question of who could bring flowing water if one's water sank away gives the hidden-water boundary to the freely gushing spring found in the garden.
luna: This retelling names Aad's destruction by a violent, barren wind, a second account of the storm the section reads into the cloud over their valley.
luna: The wind is sustained over Aad for seven nights and eight days; the next ayah records its aftermath, extending the section's brief cloud-to-destruction scene.
luna: The wind's result is that no remnant of the people is seen; this is the outcome of the prolonged Ad storm described in 69:6 and 69:7.

luna: “لَمَّا طَغَى الْمَاءُ” names water overflowing its bounds, the section's flood image; here that deluge carries people in the ship, whereas the section's overflowing violence receives a lash of punishment. | terra: إِنَّا لَمَّا طَغَا ٱلْمَآءُ recalls the Flood as water that transgressed its measure, exactly the section's way of hearing the tyrants' طغيان as a flood.

luna: Mountains are crushed with one crushing before the Day's event arrives; this places ruined terrain beside the advent that the section stages on a flattened plain. | terra: The earth and mountains are lifted and crushed دَكَّةًۭ وَٰحِدَةًۭ, a direct parallel to the doubled دك of the section's final leveling.
luna: The inevitable event occurs immediately after the crushed mountains of 69:14; the sequence parallels the section's placement of destruction and arrival on one ground.
terra: كُلُوا۟ وَٱشْرَبُوا۟ هَنِيٓـًٔۢا بِمَآ أَسْلَفْتُمْ turns what was sent ahead in former days into a feast, answering the futile wish that one had sent something ahead for true life.
luna: The condemned person is described as one who did not urge feeding the poor, repeating the section's specific rebuke about withholding encouragement to feed the needy.
luna: The next ayah says he has no close friend on that Day; this contributes the absence of human backing that the section joins to the solitary arrival.
terra: The Fire calls the person who جَمَعَ فَأَوْعَىٰ, gathering and withholding into a container; this is a concise parallel to the section's amassed heap.
terra: أُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ فِى جَنَّٰتٍۢ مُّكْرَمُونَ again locates honor inside gardens, supporting the section's relocation of honor away from amassed property.
terra: Celestial listening seats are now guarded so that anyone attempting to listen finds a flame lying in watch, a different r-s-d watchpoint in the sky.
terra: God tells the Prophet to leave Him with the person He created alone, beginning a portrait that joins original singleness to worldly accumulation.
terra: The same solitary creature is given extended wealth, so wealth sits directly beside the single-person image without overcoming it.
terra: The oath by night as it withdraws supplies the receding dark cover before morning appears in the next ayah.

luna: The oath by morning as it brightens gives another direct dawn formulation for the section's image of the first light standing out against darkness. | terra: The oath by morning as it brightens gives another direct dawn-emergence after the withdrawing night.

luna: The root's moral form appears in the wish “لِيَفْجُرَ أَمَامَهُ”; the person wants to persist in wrongdoing, a specific instance of the section's fujur tearing through religious restraint. | terra: بَلْ يُرِيدُ ٱلْإِنسَٰنُ لِيَفْجُرَ أَمَامَهُ uses the fecr branch for the human wish to keep breaching ahead, the moral sense the section locates between its first and last words.
terra: إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ يَوْمَئِذٍ ٱلْمُسْتَقَرُّ locates the final place of settling with the Lord, joining journey and true rest.
terra: بَلْ تُحِبُّونَ ٱلْعَاجِلَةَ identifies love of the immediate life, close to the section's adhesive love of wealth and earth.
terra: وَتَذَرُونَ ٱلْءَاخِرَةَ states what that immediate attachment leaves behind, defining the lost direction of travel.

luna: The section explicitly names the water sense of ف ج ر; here Allah's servants drink from a spring and “يُفَجِّرُونَهَا تَفْجِيرًا”, directing its flow as they will, a blessed counterpart to the flood of punishment. | terra: A spring drunk by God's servants is made to gush by them, يُفَجِّرُونَهَا تَفْجِيرًا; it unites the fecr-root's water branch, servants, and the gardenward destination exactly as the section says.

luna: The righteous give food to the needy, orphan, and captive despite loving it; this puts the section's orphan beside its table and turns support into a shared meal. | terra: They feed food they love to the poor, orphan, and captive; loved provision becomes a shared table rather than a hoarded pile.
terra: The feeders explain that they seek neither recompense nor thanks from those fed, distinguishing the shared table of 76:8 from wealth used to prove personal honor.
luna: The righteous are rewarded for patience with a garden; this supplies the garden setting for the section's welcomed soul and the spring image of 76:6.
luna: The garden's shade hangs close over its inhabitants and its fruit is made easy to reach; this gives a concrete canopy to the section's reading of the final word as tree-cover.
terra: Those people love ٱلْعَاجِلَةَ and leave behind a heavy day; love of what is near produces the wrong kind of heaviness in the section's journey-image.
luna: The sky's “سِرَاجًا وَهَّاجًا” is a blazing lamp, a concrete light-source parallel to the section's dictionary image of the dawn's standing column of light.

luna: Abundant water is poured from the clouds; this follows the blazing lamp in 78:13 and joins the section's light, rain, and garden images. | terra: وَأَنزَلْنَا مِنَ ٱلْمُعْصِرَٰتِ مَآءً ثَجَّاجًا presents the hoped-for counterpart: abundant water descending from rain clouds rather than a scourge descending as punishment.
luna: The poured water brings grain and plants; this completes the provision begun in 78:14 and shows water becoming sustenance rather than punishment.
luna: The same water sequence produces lush gardens; this neighboring culmination connects the section's cloud and garden meeting.
terra: The mountains are set moving until they are a mirage; within the same surah Hell becomes مرصاد and the angels later stand in a row, so this ayah supplies the cleared terrain of that meeting.

luna: Hell is named “مِرْصَادًا”, an ambush or watchpoint; this is the same waiting-place image the section hears in its word for God's watch over the transgressors. | terra: إِنَّ جَهَنَّمَ كَانَتْ مِرْصَادًا names Hell itself as a watchpoint, the compulsory ambush-place through which the section hears retribution arrive.
luna: The next verse names the transgressors as Hell's destination; it specifies whom the ambush of 78:21 awaits, as the section connects watchfulness with punishment.

luna: On the Day of the Spirit and angels standing in ranks, the same rowed assembly arrives on a judgment scene, matching the section's angels lined across the leveled ground. | terra: The Spirit and angels stand صَفًّا before the Merciful, directly matching the ranks that remain upright on the leveled ground.

terra: فَأَمَّا مَن طَغَىٰ opens a sequence in which transgression, preference for the nearer life, punishment, restraint of the soul, and garden are set against one another, closely recapitulating the section's arc.
terra: وَءَاثَرَ ٱلْحَيَوٰةَ ٱلدُّنْيَا names preference for the lower life as the transgressor's decisive choice, corresponding to the section's earthbound satisfaction.
terra: فَإِنَّ ٱلْجَحِيمَ هِىَ ٱلْمَأْوَىٰ gives the preferred lower life's destination, completing the negative half of the 79:37-41 contrast.
terra: The opposite person fears standing before the Lord and restrains ٱلنَّفْسَ from desire; the soul now moves toward its Lord rather than settling into appetite.
terra: فَإِنَّ ٱلْجَنَّةَ هِىَ ٱلْمَأْوَىٰ completes the reversal by making the garden, rather than the lower life, the soul's abiding place.

luna: The same root ص ب ب appears in “صَبَبْنَا الْمَاءَ صَبًّا” for poured rain; the next verses show it yielding food, the life-giving water action set against the section's poured punishment. | terra: أَنَّا صَبَبْنَا ٱلْمَآءَ صَبًّا states the ordinary water-action behind the section's startling use of pouring for a scourge.

luna: On the Day each person flees from his brother; the following verses extend the separation through parents, spouse, and children, giving social detail to the section's unsupported single arrival.
luna: Flight from one's mother and father extends the separation begun in 80:34; the scene makes the absence of human backing concrete.
luna: Flight from spouse and children continues the same Day-of-judgment separation, adding the closest household ties to the solitary scene.
luna: Each person is occupied with his own concern; this completes the family-flight passage and explains the section's image of no one standing behind the solitary person.
terra: The retreating night supplies the covering that is being withdrawn immediately before the morning breathes in 81:18.

luna: The oath “وَالصُّبْحِ إِذَا تَنَفَّسَ” pictures morning breathing; it extends the section's dawn as a force that opens darkness. | terra: وَٱلصُّبْحِ إِذَا تَنَفَّسَ personifies morning emerging after retreating night, a close parallel to dawn opening the dark cover.
terra: وَإِذَا ٱلْبِحَارُ فُجِّرَتْ applies the fecr branch to waters bursting open at the last upheaval, the catastrophic boundary to the measured garden spring.
terra: The human is asked what deceived him concerning his generous Lord, redirecting the honor-question from possessions toward the giver and human self-deception.
terra: The righteous are in bliss immediately before the wicked are placed in Hell, supplying the positive half of the fujjar boundary.

luna: The “فُجَّار” are placed in Hell; this uses the same moral word named by the section and connects transgression to its judgment landscape. | terra: وَإِنَّ ٱلْفُجَّارَ لَفِى جَحِيمٍ gives the moral f-j-r branch its final destination in direct contrast with 82:13.
terra: No soul will possess anything for another on that day, expressing the absence of interpersonal support behind the image of each person's solitary arrival.
luna: The section reads moral فُجُور as tearing a religious cover; here accumulated wrongdoing leaves a rusting layer over hearts, an inverse covering image that marks the two outcomes of sin.
terra: When the earth is stretched flat, it supplies another direct Quranic scene for the leveled ground of the final arrival.
terra: Humanity is described as laboring toward its Lord and then meeting Him, making life a journey whose destination is the return-call's speaker.
terra: بَلْ تُؤْثِرُونَ ٱلْحَيَوٰةَ ٱلدُّنْيَا names the preference that makes a person settle into the lower life rather than answer the return-call.
terra: وَٱلْءَاخِرَةُ خَيْرٌ وَأَبْقَىٰ sets what is better and lasting against the lower life preferred in 87:16, clarifying the destination of the return.
terra: فِيهَا عَيْنٌ جَارِيَةٌ places a flowing spring inside the high garden, a concise parallel to the water found after the soul enters.

luna: The difficult ascent is feeding someone on a day of hunger; 90:15 and 90:16 specify the orphan and destitute, completing the food scene that meets the section's orphan image. | terra: أَوْ إِطْعَٰمٌ فِى يَوْمٍۢ ذِى مَسْغَبَةٍ makes feeding during hunger the difficult liberating act, opened toward the orphan in 90:15.

luna: The hungry person is an orphan close in kin; this places the orphan directly inside the feeding scene begun in 90:14 and continued in 90:16. | terra: يَتِيمًا ذَا مَقْرَبَةٍ makes a related orphan the first person seated at that figurative table.

luna: The next person named is one in misery and dust; together with 90:14 and 90:15 this completes the passage's concrete call to feed the vulnerable. | terra: أَوْ مِسْكِينًا ذَا مَتْرَبَةٍ adds the poor person lying in dust, closely echoing the section's orphan-and-poor pairing.

luna: After feeding the hungry and naming the orphan and destitute, the passage describes a community that urges patience and compassion; this connects the shared table to the section's soul joining God's servants.

luna: Day is sworn by as it reveals, paired with night that covers in 91:4; this mirrors the section's meeting of dawn breaking one cover and a garden as another. | terra: Day is sworn by when it displays the sun, contributing the unveiling half of the cover-and-opening relation.

luna: Night is “إِذَا يَغْشَىٰهَا”, covering the day; its contrast with 91:3 sharpens the section's image of dawn splitting darkness. | terra: Night is sworn by when it covers the sun, naming the veil whose removal 91:3 implies.

luna: The source section names فُجُور as moral violation; here “فُجُورَهَا” is paired with taqwa as the soul's contrary moral capacities, preserving the section's link between opening and transgression. | terra: فَأَلْهَمَهَا فُجُورَهَا وَتَقْوَىٰهَا names فجور within the soul and sets it against piety, supporting the section's moral breach between fecr's opening and garden's cover.
terra: God دَمْدَمَ عَلَيْهِمْ and سَوَّىٰهَا against Thamud; the named people, crushing punishment, and leveling meet, though the object of leveling admits more than one reading.
terra: وَٱلَّيْلِ إِذَا يَغْشَىٰ explicitly makes night a covering, the surface the section says dawn rends.
terra: وَٱلنَّهَارِ إِذَا تَجَلَّىٰ makes daylight's unveiling the counterpart to night covering in 92:1.
terra: The God-fearing person gives his wealth to purify himself, reversing adhesive love and preparing the satisfaction promised in 92:21.
terra: وَلَسَوْفَ يَرْضَىٰ promises satisfaction to the wealth-giver, locating رضى after release of wealth rather than its accumulation.
terra: The bright forenoon is paired by oath with the still night, another juxtaposition of emerging light and dark repose.
terra: Night when it grows still supplies the low, quiet condition that the following reassurance prevents from being mistaken for abandonment.
terra: أَلَمْ يَجِدْكَ يَتِيمًا فَـَٔاوَىٰ answers orphan singleness with shelter, a concrete form of drawing the unsupported person alongside.

luna: The orphan is explicitly not to be oppressed; this is a direct moral reversal of abandoning the lone child whom the section says should be honored. | terra: فَأَمَّا ٱلْيَتِيمَ فَلَا تَقْهَرْ turns remembered shelter into a direct command not to overpower the orphan.
terra: إِنَّ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ ٱلرُّجْعَىٰ states the journey's endpoint in the same return language as the call to the tranquil soul.

luna: The reward is gardens with God pleased with them and they pleased with Him; this closely matches the section's “رَاضِيَةً مَرْضِيَّةً” and its reciprocal return. | terra: رَّضِىَ ٱللَّهُ عَنْهُمْ وَرَضُوا۟ عَنْهُ appears with abiding gardens, exactly expanding the section's reciprocal رَاضِيَةً مَّرْضِيَّةً and garden entry.
luna: The earth is violently shaken at the final hour; this repeats the upheaval that precedes the section's calm soul and assembly.
luna: The earth brings its burdens out after the shaking; this continues 99:1's scene and gives the upheaval a visible result.
luna: Competition in accumulating more distracts people; it directly parallels the section's image of loving wealth as an ever-growing heap.
luna: The competition lasts until people visit the graves; this completes 102:1 and shows the limit of the accumulating that the section says cannot save.

luna: The person “الَّذِي جَمَعَ مَالًا وَعَدَّدَهُ” piles up and counts wealth, the heap paired by the section with the upright columns of 104:9. | terra: ٱلَّذِى جَمَعَ مَالًا وَعَدَّدَهُ identifies the same wealth-gatherer whose horizontal heap the section sets beside raised columns.

luna: This person's belief that wealth will make him last forever completes the portrait begun in 104:2; it supports the section's claim that neither piling wealth nor erecting columns saves their owner. | terra: He calculates that his wealth has made him immortal; the claim states why his amassed pile seems protective before the surah turns it into confinement.
terra: The wealth-counter is thrown into the Crusher, turning the confidence of 104:3 toward the enclosure by extended columns in 104:8-9.
terra: إِنَّهَا عَلَيْهِم مُّؤْصَدَةٌ makes the Fire close over the wealth-counter, clarifying what the extended columns of 104:9 do to him.

luna: The source section names the dictionary sense “extended columns” (عَمَدٍ مُمَدَّدَةٍ); this verse uses that exact phrase for the confinement of the wealth-hoarder, joining its pillar image to his gathered wealth. | terra: فِى عَمَدٍۢ مُّمَدَّدَةٍۭ is the section's explicit second column scene: amassed wealth cannot save its builder from enclosure within extended columns.

luna: The denier of judgment repels the orphan, the opposite of the section's call to honor and draw near to him. | terra: فَذَٰلِكَ ٱلَّذِى يَدُعُّ ٱلْيَتِيمَ identifies denial by the act of pushing the orphan away, the direct opposite of coming alongside the one left alone.

luna: He does not encourage feeding the poor; this neighboring rebuke completes 107:2's treatment of the orphan and reverses the section's table and care images. | terra: وَلَا يَحُضُّ عَلَىٰ طَعَامِ ٱلْمِسْكِينِ repeats beside the orphan the same failure to urge feeding that follows it in the section.
